topics.title: Chapter overview
topics.summary: A network endpoint combines addressing, transport, and application protocol choices. A listening socket is not a complete service contract, and name resolution is not proof of reachability. This chapter builds a numeric loopback endpoint without contacting an external DNS server, inspects its normalized host and service strings, and opens a local listener on an operating-system-selected port.

blocks.text: A client reports that “the network is down.” The server is listening, but only on the loopback address of another machine. Name resolution succeeds, the route exists, and the application is healthy; the configured endpoint does not provide the path the client expected. Effective network diagnosis follows the request across layers rather than treating every failed connection as the same problem.

That deliberately narrow environment lets you verify the socket interface before adding infrastructure dependencies.

topics.title: 14.1.2 Understanding Ports and Transport Protocols
topics.summary: Ports distinguish transport endpoints for protocols such as TCP and UDP. The same numeric port under different transport protocols is not the same socket endpoint. TCP provides an ordered byte stream with connection semantics; UDP provides datagrams without the same delivery or ordering guarantee.

cards.question: Explain Understanding Ports and Transport Protocols in your own words.
cards.answer: Ports distinguish transport endpoints for protocols such as TCP and UDP. The same numeric port under different transport protocols is not the same socket endpoint. TCP provides an ordered byte stream with connection semantics; UDP provides datagrams without the same delivery or ordering guarantee.

A service must agree with its clients about address family, address, transport, port, and application protocol. Matching only the number shown in a configuration file is insufficient.

blocks.text: TCP provides a reliable ordered byte-stream abstraction while a connection is functioning, but it does not preserve application write boundaries or guarantee that a remote application committed a request. UDP preserves datagram boundaries but does not provide delivery, ordering, or duplicate suppression as an application guarantee. These differences affect parser design, retry behavior, and the evidence needed to acknowledge work.

blocks.text: A listening TCP socket is not a connected client socket. The listener accepts connection attempts; each successful accept creates a new socket for a particular connection. The server retains the listener if it intends to accept more clients, while ownership of each accepted descriptor can move to a worker. Closing one accepted connection need not stop the listener, and closing the listener does not automatically define cleanup for every accepted socket.

blocks.text: Binding port zero asks the operating system to select an available local port. After binding, query the actual assigned endpoint rather than assuming zero is the port clients should use. This is useful in tests because it avoids choosing a fixed port that may already be occupied. It does not eliminate all resource limits or make concurrent tests immune to every environmental failure.

reading.title: 14.2.2 Resolving Names and Addresses
paragraphs: getaddrinfo converts a host and service description into candidate address structures under supplied hints. It reports errors through its own error-code interface rather than always through errno. The returned linked result list must be released with freeaddrinfo, and its nodes remain valid only until that release.

Numeric-only flags can prevent DNS resolution when the input is already a literal address and port. That is useful for a deterministic fixture. A real hostname-based client needs a policy for result ordering, address-family fallback, connection deadlines, and resolver failure. A successful lookup establishes candidate addresses, not that a server is listening or authorized.

Name and service resolution translates human-oriented inputs into candidate socket addresses. getaddrinfo returns a linked collection of results and an error channel distinct from ordinary errno-based system calls. Each result includes the family, socket type, protocol, address, and length needed for a compatible socket attempt. Free the returned collection using its matching release function. (GETADDRINFO)

The example sets numeric-host and numeric-service flags. That makes 127.0.0.1 and 8080 explicit numeric inputs and avoids DNS or service-name lookup. Successful execution therefore establishes the numeric conversion path, not the health of a DNS resolver. This distinction belongs in the test report because a local deterministic fixture should not be presented as a network-infrastructure validation.
